Commentary.Commentary: We are back. Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill to open for India. Lockie Ferguson to bowl first.
...THE CHASE...

New Zealand batters came and went just like a tourist does. This is a really disappointing performance from them. The top 5 went for a single-digit. Michael Bracewell and Glenn Phillips joined hands and restored things but only for a short period as the former fell. Mitchell Santner then joined but he too fell. Glenn Phillips batted brilliantly and probably had a really good chance to help his team but his soft dismissal didn't help and his wicket meant New Zealand end under 110 runs. Someone who bets New Zealand to win from here will be a very brave person. Stay tuned.

What a bowling performance by India! The bat did all the talk in the first match and it was time for the bowlers to shine up and boy they did. However, it was all possible because of the fiery opening spell from Siraj and Shami. They both were so disciplined and extracted everything the pitch had to offer. In no time, they dusted New Zealand three down inside the 10 overs. Then, Thakur and Pandya put on a show and they too keep the good work on and put New Zealand at bay. There were two stands but overall, this total should not trouble India at all. Prime bowling performance by India. They will be really proud of it.

India (UNCHANGED PLAYING XI) - Rohit Sharma (C), Shubman Gill, Virat Kohli, Ishan Kishan (WK), Suryakumar Yadav, Hardik Pandya, Washington Sundar, Shardul Thakur, Kuldeep Yadav, Mohammad Shami, Mohammed Siraj.

Tom Latham says they would have bowled first. Reckons he is unsure how the pitch will play. Admits there were a lot of positives from the first game. Tells the young players need experience and they are excited about the opportunity. Shares they are playing the same team.

Rohit Sharma surprisingly forgets what they will do but eventually makes the call and decides to bowl first. Adds the wicket gets better to bowl on when the light comes on. Reckons dew might play a part but the curators says dew doesn't arrive on game day so they are not thinking much. Shares there are playing the same team.
TOSS - India have won the toss and will BOWL first!

The road to the 2023 ODI World Cup continues, and we shift our focus to another tasty clash between India and New Zealand in this three-match series. The 2nd ODI will be played at the Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Stadium in Raipur, India, and if the first game was anything to go by, we are in for another thrilling game. It was the Gill-Bracewell show in the first match, and the fans will expect another run-fest. India recently whitewashed their neighbours Sri Lanka in this format, and they started this series with a win too, but only just. The star of the act was Shubman Gill, with his magnificent double century, who became the tenth player to achieve that feat and the fifth Indian to do so. However, there was a point when it looked like he wouldn't be on the winning side when Michael Bracewell and Mitchell Santner were punishing the Indian bowlers. Except for Gill, only Rohit Sharma and Suryakumar Yadav were able to cross the 30-run mark, which is a bit of a worry for them. Their batters will need to convert their starts into big scores, as nowadays we have seen enough evidence that no total is safe enough. Virat Kohli will want to get some runs and maintain his good run to avoid going into another lean patch. While defending a high total, Indian bowling was not up to the mark, especially against the lower middle order of the Kiwis. This has been a problem for India in recent times, except for the third ODI against Sri Lanka, as they concede too many runs to the tail and find it difficult to wrap up their opponents. Mohammad Shami hasn't looked like himself and may need some time off, and they could use the express pace of Umran Malik in this game. Mohammed Siraj continued his good form, and Kuldeep Yadav is doing all the right things at the moment. They got out of jail in the first game, but they will need to work on their bowling to get another victory over the Kiwis and seal the series. New Zealand, on the other hand, showed why they are the top-ranked ODI side. They also came into this series after playing some really good cricket in the sub-continent and beating Pakistan in a three-match ODI series. New Zealand looked down and out at one stage, chasing a huge score, but Michael Bracewell stepped up once again for them and smashed the Indian bowlers all around the park. However, he only got support from Mitchell Santner, and in the end, he failed to take his side over the line. He bludgeoned 140 runs and almost single-handedly won the game for them. The Kiwis are missing some of the key players like Southee, Boult, and Williamson, and that reflected in their performance, especially in their bowling department. Their top order also failed to perform, and they will need more from Finn Allen and Devon Conway. They can make a few changes and bring in Doug Bracewell, who can contribute with some medium pace and bat down the order, while they can also try Ish Sodhi to give them another spin option. They will have the confidence in them as they know they gave a huge scare to the Indian team, and if they improve in some areas, they can get the win here. Also, they are top of the ICC Super League table and will want to strengthen their position, while Super League points won't matter for India as they are the hosts for the upcoming World Cup. Will the Kiwis fight back to level the series? Or will the Men in Blue wrap this up with one game to spare? Let's find out together.
